entries.locator: Lecture beat 1: two routes into fields, changing particle number, one-species scope, and deliberate pacing
entries.note: The opening motivation, room-photon and beta-decay examples, and abstract-but-elementary pacing are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 2: one-particle wavefunction, Born density, normalization, basis choice, and box modes
entries.note: Lower-case wavefunction notation and its accidental one-particle number interpretation are kept distinct from the field.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 3: Born-rule question, resolution of identity, and position-space completeness
entries.note: The star-placement correction and delta-function derivation are preserved.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 4: occupation-number states, larger Hilbert space, oscillator bookkeeping, and Fock space
entries.note: The notes explicitly separate one-particle states from Fock-space states.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 5: field mode expansions, Fourier analogy, Hermitian combinations, and operator-valued position dependence
entries.note: Capital fields, lower-case modes, c-numbers, q-numbers, and observable combinations are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 6: vacuum, resolution of identity, local creation, dagger correction, and commuting mode functions
entries.note: The derivation of Psi-dagger(x)|0> = |x> is kept step by step.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 7: total-number derivation and local particle-density operator
entries.note: The double sum, orthogonality reduction, regional measurement, and fluctuations are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 8: operator domain, density-versus-probability, general superpositions, and charge conservation
entries.note: All three extended classroom exchanges are represented as Q&A blocks.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 9: independent-particle approximation, dilute systems, modes, and the energy sum
entries.note: The photon-interaction qualification and meaning of omega_i are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 10: one-particle Schrodinger eigenvalue equation and momentum as a differential operator
entries.note: Both one-dimensional p=-i partial_x and three-dimensional Laplacian forms are typeset and frame-backed.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 11: one-particle energy expectation and the guessed field Hamiltonian
entries.note: The lecture's answer-first, proof-second order is preserved.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 12: mode-expansion proof of the field Hamiltonian
entries.note: The differential operator action, eigenvalue substitution, orthogonality integral, and final mode sum are complete.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 13: why the operator-valued function is a field and how its quanta identify the species
entries.note: The nonrelativistic scope and electromagnetic comparison are explicit.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 14: local energy density, regional integration, and operator versus eigenvalue notation
entries.note: The density ambiguity, capital N versus lower-case n, and bra-ket distinction are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 15: recovery of one-particle quantum mechanics and the classical-field limit
entries.note: The one-particle sector and time-dependent Schrodinger behavior of suitable expectation values are included.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 16: why the Hamiltonian derivation did not illegally commute operators
entries.note: The distinction between derivatives on mode functions and operators on Fock states is preserved.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 17: early wave-particle confusion and the Dirac-notation mathematics-department anecdote
entries.note: The anecdote is condensed without importing the lecture's unsupported personal diagnosis.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 18: fields as measurable quantum-particle structure rather than empty formalism
entries.note: Interference and entanglement are retained as the physical content of the formalism.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 19: relativistic localization caveat and the E+iB electromagnetic aside
entries.note: The energy-density interpretation is kept separate from a literal photon probability density.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 20: reversed field ordering and the additive ground-state contribution
entries.note: The normal-ordering caveat is included without extending into a full vacuum-energy treatment.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 21: one-particle momentum expectation, total field momentum, and operator versus expectation value
entries.note: The laser momentum example and final state/operator distinction are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 22: natural stopping point and preview of decay and scattering
entries.note: The chapter closes with the lecture's stated next step rather than an imposed summary.
